question: How many tonnes of pizza do people in Chicago eat on an average day in 2026?

target.what: Total mass of pizza consumed by people in Chicago (city of Chicago, Illinois) on an average day in 2026, counting all pizza eaten by residents and visitors within the city, including restaurant/takeout/delivery and home-prepared pizza, measured as prepared pizza mass (not dough or ingredients)
target.cadence: Annual average daily rate, not a published series
target.caveats: Ambiguous scope: 'people in Chicago' could mean residents only (population ~2.7M) or all persons present including commuters and tourists (~3.5-4M person-days). Working interpretation: all pizza consumed within Chicago city limits on an average day, by residents plus visitors/commuters present. Excl

candidates.hypothesis: US per-capita pizza consumption (kg/person/year) multiplied by Chicago's effective person-days gives total consumption; Chicago's pizza culture likely raises its per-capita rate above the national average by a transferable multiplier.
candidates.data_to_find: US annual pizza consumption or sales volume in tonnes (or USD sales converted via average price per pizza), US population, and any Chicago-vs-national pizza consumption or restaurant-density index. Minimum: one national per-capita pizza mass figure and a Chicago adjustment factor.
search_hints: US pizza consumption per capita pounds per year
pizza industry statistics annual sales volume tons
Chicago pizza consumption per capita vs national

candidates.hypothesis: Number of pizzerias in Chicago × average daily pizzas sold per shop × average pizza mass = commercial pizza mass; add non-pizzeria pizza sales and homemade.
candidates.data_to_find: Count of Chicago pizzerias/pizza-serving restaurants, average daily pizza orders per store (or annual revenue per store divided by average ticket), average pizza weight in kg. Minimum: pizzeria count and a per-store daily pizza volume.
search_hints: average pizzas sold per pizzeria per day

candidates.hypothesis: Pizza mass consumed = dough/flour and cheese throughput into Chicago pizza production × conversion yield; cheese or flour shipments to Chicago food service bound pizza output.
candidates.data_to_find: Chicago-area food-service cheese or pizza-flour shipments/consumption, or mozzarella production attributable to Chicago; conversion factors (kg cheese per kg pizza, kg flour per kg pizza). Minimum: one input flow plus a yield ratio.

candidates.hypothesis: Share of person-days on which pizza is eaten × average mass per pizza-eating occasion × effective population present = daily pizza mass.
candidates.data_to_find: US pizza eating frequency (e.g., % of adults eating pizza on a given day from NHANES/CDC), average grams of pizza per eating occasion, and Chicago effective population/person-days. Minimum: frequency and grams-per-occasion.
search_hints: NHANES pizza consumption frequency grams per day
percentage of Americans eat pizza on a given day
average pizza serving size grams survey

candidates.hypothesis: Chicago pizza restaurant sales (USD/day) divided by average price per pizza and multiplied by average pizza mass gives commercial pizza mass; adjust for non-restaurant channels.
candidates.data_to_find: Chicago metro pizza restaurant annual sales or limited-service pizza sales, average pizza price in Chicago, average pizza weight. Minimum: Chicago pizza sales total and price-per-pizza.
search_hints: Chicago pizza restaurant sales revenue annual

candidates.hypothesis: Effective person-days in Chicago = residents + commuters + tourists; pizza consumption scales with person-days, so tourist and commuter shares materially change the total.
candidates.data_to_find: Chicago resident population 2026, daily commuter inflow, annual visitor count and average stay, to compute average daily persons present. Minimum: resident population and net daily visitor/commuter person-days.
search_hints: Chicago tourism visitors annual 2025 average stay

candidates.hypothesis: If any prior estimate of Chicago pizza consumption or sales exists, extrapolate to 2026 using population and price/volume growth; otherwise use national pizza sales growth as a proxy trend.
candidates.data_to_find: Any published Chicago pizza consumption/sales estimate for earlier years, and US pizza sales growth rates 2020-2025. Minimum: one historical anchor or a growth rate to apply to a current-year base.

candidates.hypothesis: Day-of-week and seasonal effects (weekends, holidays, sports events) shift daily pizza mass; an 'average day' should weight these, and 2026-specific events (e.g., major conventions, sports playoffs) could raise the average.
candidates.data_to_find: Day-of-week and seasonal variation in pizza sales, Chicago 2026 major events/conventions calendar, and any measurable event-driven pizza demand spikes. Minimum: a weekday/weekend ratio and event calendar.
search_hints: pizza sales day of week variation

params.formula: a3 * p33 * a2 * mean(p35, p36) * p37 * a1 * k_days_per_year / 1000

a3.role: Chicago effective person-days present on an average day in 2026

p33.role: US share of population 2+ consuming pizza on any given day (NHANES 2017–2020), transferred to Chicago

a2.role: Chicago pizza-culture multiplier on the national any-day occasion rate

p35.role: average slices per pizza-eating occasion, males (NHANES)

p36.role: average slices per pizza-eating occasion, females (NHANES)

p37.role: fraction of a 14-inch pizza per slice (reference slice definition)

a1.role: grams per reference slice, converting slice fractions to prepared mass

methods.rationale: d3 base-rate route: effective person-days × any-day pizza share × Chicago uplift × mean slices per occasion × slice fraction × grams per slice. The k_days_per_year/1000 factor converts the per-occasion gram chain into a daily tonne rate (the formula as written yields grams per day before scaling; declared unit t/day after the /1000). Key dependencies: NHANES is US-wide and 2017–2020, so a2 and a3 carry the transfer; a1 carries the slice-to-mass conversion. Failure mode: if Chicago occasion rates or slice weights differ sharply from national, the estimate shifts proportionally.

p18.role: count of pizza restaurants in Chicago, 2026-04-01

a4.role: prepared mass per whole commercial pizza in kg

a5.role: share of total pizza mass from non-pizzeria channels, used to gross up pizzeria mass

p46.role: Chicago DMA pizza orders per month per respondent, used as a per-restaurant monthly order proxy

methods.rationale: d2/d4 capacity-times-utilisation route: restaurant count × mass per pizza × orders per restaurant per month ÷ days per month, grossed up for non-pizzeria channels. The p46 per-respondent order rate is a household-level survey figure, not a per-restaurant figure; using it as a per-restaurant monthly order count is a strong transfer assumption that likely overstates per-shop volume (a respondent orders for a household, a shop serves many households). This method is therefore a rough cross-check rather than a primary estimate; its main value is bounding the commercial channel. Failure modes: p18 list may include non-pizza-focused restaurants; a4 and a5 are broad assumptions.

assumptions.name: Grams per NHANES reference slice
assumptions.rationale: A 1/6 slice of a 14-inch regular-crust cheese pizza (p37) typically weighs roughly 90–130 g; deep-dish and heavily topped slices run higher. Midpoint ~110 g with a wide range reflects style mix in Chicago, where deep-dish is over-represented relative to the national NHANES sample.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert NHANES slice counts (p35, p36) into prepared pizza mass for the d3 occasion route.
assumptions.falsified_by: A measured average slice weight for US restaurant pizza materially outside 75–160 g.

assumptions.name: Chicago pizza-culture multiplier on national occasion rate
assumptions.rationale: Chicago's pizza identity (deep-dish, tavern-style, high pizzeria density) plausibly lifts per-person pizza occasions above the national 11% any-day rate (p33). The survey shows Chicago DMA orders 5.66/month vs national ~5 (p46 vs p48), a ~13% premium, supporting a modest uplift rather than a large one.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to the national any-day pizza-consumption share when transferring to Chicago person-days.
assumptions.falsified_by: Local Chicago dietary-recall data showing pizza occasion rates at or below the national 11%.

assumptions.name: Chicago effective person-days (residents + commuters + visitors)
assumptions.rationale: Chicago residents ~2.7M plus net commuter inflow and visitor-days. 1990 CTPP showed large suburban inflow (p83–p86); modern inflow is smaller but still material. Visitors (~57M/year, p69) with ~2-night stays add roughly 0.3M person-days/day. Range spans residents-only to a generous commuter+visitor inclusion.
assumptions.applies_when: Denominator for the d3/d6 exposure route; represents all persons eating within city limits on an average day.
assumptions.falsified_by: Current ACS population plus LEHD commuter inflow implying effective person-days outside 2.9–3.8M.

assumptions.name: Prepared mass per whole pizza (commercial)
assumptions.rationale: A typical 14-inch thin-crust pizza weighs ~0.7–0.9 kg; deep-dish and large chain pizzas run 1.2–1.5 kg. Chicago's style mix (deep-dish plus tavern thin) centers near 1 kg. Used to convert pizzeria order counts into mass in the d4 route.
assumptions.applies_when: Converts Chicago DMA pizza orders (p46) into prepared pizza mass.
assumptions.falsified_by: Measured average whole-pizza weight for Chicago commercial pizzas outside 0.7–1.4 kg.

assumptions.name: Share of Chicago pizza mass from non-pizzeria channels (grocery/frozen, home-made, other)
assumptions.rationale: NHANES shows ~6% from 'other' sources (p41) but that excludes supermarket frozen/refrigerated pizza eaten at home, which is a large share of US pizza intake. Restaurant/pizzeria channels likely supply 50–80% of pizza mass; 35% non-pizzeria is a central allowance.
assumptions.applies_when: Grosses up pizzeria-channel mass (m2) to total pizza mass including retail and home-prepared.
assumptions.falsified_by: Chicago retail scanner data showing frozen/refrigerated pizza share far from 20–50% of total pizza mass.

methods.rationale: Exposure-times-rate route: national per-capita pizza mass (p146) times Chicago residents (p202), uplifted for Chicago pizza culture (a1) and for commuters/visitors present (a3), divided by days per year. Failure modes: the national per-capita figure is an unsourced web compilation and may already embed Chicago; the culture multiplier and person-day uplift are judgment calls. Shared dependency with m2 on the same underlying consumption concept.

p33.role: share of US population 2+ consuming pizza on any given day (NHANES)

p202.role: City of Chicago resident population, 2024 ACS

a3.role: effective person-days in Chicago relative to resident population

a2.role: average prepared pizza mass per pizza-eating occasion

methods.rationale: Occasion route: NHANES daily pizza-consumption share (p33) times effective person-days (p202 x a3) times average mass per occasion (a2). The NHANES share is national and 2017-2020; it is transferred to Chicago 2026 without a trend adjustment because no per-capita trend series is kept. Failure modes: a2 is the dominant uncertainty (slice size varies by crust style), and the NHANES share may understate Chicago's pizza-heavy culture. Shares the a3 person-day uplift with m1.

p18.role: count of pizza restaurants in Chicago, April 2026

a5.role: average pizzas sold per pizzeria per day

a4.role: average prepared pizza mass per pizza sold

methods.rationale: Capacity/throughput route: pizzeria count (p18) times daily pies per shop (a5) times mass per pie (a4), grossed up for non-pizzeria channels (a6). Failure modes: p18 is a directory count that may include chains and non-pizza-focused restaurants; a5 is a planning assumption, not measured Chicago sales; a6 is derived from a national NHANES source split. This route is structurally independent of m1/m2 (it uses restaurant counts rather than per-capita rates), so it provides a useful cross-check.

assumptions.name: Chicago pizza-culture multiplier on national per-capita pizza consumption
assumptions.rationale: Chicago is a nationally recognized pizza city (deep-dish, tavern-style) with a dense pizzeria count (p18: 1,987 restaurants for ~2.7M residents, roughly 73 per 100k, well above typical US city densities). A modest 10-35% uplift over the national per-capita rate is plausible; the low end allows no uplift because the national figure already includes Chicago.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to transfer the US per-capita pizza consumption rate (p146) to Chicago residents.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that Chicago per-capita pizza sales or consumption are at or below the national average.

assumptions.name: Average prepared pizza mass per pizza-eating occasion
assumptions.rationale: NHANES gives 3-4 slices per occasion (p35/p36) and a slice is 1/6 of a 14-inch pie (p37) weighing 853 g (p158), implying ~430-570 g for regular crust; but many occasions are thin-crust (70 g slices, p187) or smaller portions, and some occasions are snacks. A central 350 g with a wide range brackets thin-crust and deep-dish mixes.
assumptions.applies_when: Used with the NHANES occasion share to convert eating occasions to pizza mass.
assumptions.falsified_by: Measured average grams per pizza-eating occasion in a US dietary survey materially outside 220-550 g.

assumptions.name: Effective person-days in Chicago relative to resident population (commuter and visitor uplift)
assumptions.rationale: Chicago has substantial net commuter inflow (1.08M commuters, p206, many from outside the city) and ~11.9M hotel room nights (p217) plus day-trippers. Netting out residents who leave and weighting by time present, a 5-22% uplift over the resident population is a reasonable central 12%.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to scale resident-based consumption to all persons present in Chicago on an average day.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that net commuter/visitor person-days are below 5% or above 22% of resident person-days.

assumptions.name: Average prepared pizza mass per pizza sold at a Chicago pizzeria
assumptions.rationale: A 14-inch regular-crust cheese pie weighs 853 g (p158); thin-crust is lighter (~560 g at 70 g x 8 slices, p187) and deep-dish heavier (~780 g for 9-inch, p176). A central 1.0 kg with a 0.7-1.4 kg range reflects the Chicago mix of tavern-style, deep-dish, and chain pies.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert pizzeria pizza counts to mass in the capacity route.
assumptions.falsified_by: Measured average whole-pizza weight in Chicago pizzerias outside 0.7-1.4 kg.

assumptions.name: Average pizzas sold per Chicago pizzeria per day
assumptions.rationale: A typical independent pizzeria sells on the order of several dozen pies per day; chains and high-volume deep-dish tourist spots sell more, small neighborhood shops fewer. 60/day with a 35-100 range is a standard industry planning figure for urban pizzerias.
assumptions.applies_when: Used with the pizzeria count (p18) to estimate commercial pizza output.

kept.name: Chicago pizza-culture multiplier on national per-capita pizza consumption
kept.rationale: Chicago is a nationally recognized pizza city (deep-dish, tavern-style) with a dense pizzeria count (p18: 1,987 restaurants for ~2.7M residents, roughly 73 per 100k, well above typical US city densities). A modest 10-35% uplift over the national per-capita rate is plausible; the low end allows no up
kept.applies_when: Used to transfer the US per-capita pizza consumption rate (p146) to Chicago residents.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that Chicago per-capita pizza sales or consumption are at or below the national average.

kept.name: Average prepared pizza mass per pizza-eating occasion
kept.rationale: NHANES gives 3-4 slices per occasion (p35/p36) and a slice is 1/6 of a 14-inch pie (p37) weighing 853 g (p158), implying ~430-570 g for regular crust; but many occasions are thin-crust (70 g slices, p187) or smaller portions, and some occasions are snacks. A central 350 g with a wide range brackets
kept.applies_when: Used with the NHANES occasion share to convert eating occasions to pizza mass.
kept.falsified_by: Measured average grams per pizza-eating occasion in a US dietary survey materially outside 220-550 g.

kept.name: Effective person-days in Chicago relative to resident population (commuter and visitor uplift)
kept.rationale: Chicago has substantial net commuter inflow (1.08M commuters, p206, many from outside the city) and ~11.9M hotel room nights (p217) plus day-trippers. Netting out residents who leave and weighting by time present, a 5-22% uplift over the resident population is a reasonable central 12%.
kept.applies_when: Used to scale resident-based consumption to all persons present in Chicago on an average day.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that net commuter/visitor person-days are below 5% or above 22% of resident person-days.

kept.name: Average prepared pizza mass per pizza sold at a Chicago pizzeria
kept.rationale: A 14-inch regular-crust cheese pie weighs 853 g (p158); thin-crust is lighter (~560 g at 70 g x 8 slices, p187) and deep-dish heavier (~780 g for 9-inch, p176). A central 1.0 kg with a 0.7-1.4 kg range reflects the Chicago mix of tavern-style, deep-dish, and chain pies.
kept.applies_when: Used to convert pizzeria pizza counts to mass in the capacity route.
kept.falsified_by: Measured average whole-pizza weight in Chicago pizzerias outside 0.7-1.4 kg.

kept.name: Average pizzas sold per Chicago pizzeria per day
kept.rationale: A typical independent pizzeria sells on the order of several dozen pies per day; chains and high-volume deep-dish tourist spots sell more, small neighborhood shops fewer. 60/day with a 35-100 range is a standard industry planning figure for urban pizzerias.
kept.applies_when: Used with the pizzeria count (p18) to estimate commercial pizza output.
kept.falsified_by: Survey evidence that Chicago pizzerias average below 35 or above 100 pizzas per day.

kept.name: Share of Chicago pizza mass from non-pizzeria channels (grocery/frozen, home-prepared, school, other)
kept.rationale: NHANES source split (p129/p130/p131) shows 56% restaurant, 26% grocery, 12% school, 6% other; restaurant includes non-pizzeria restaurants, so the pizzeria-only share is below 56%. A 35% non-pizzeria share (grocery + home + school + other, net of non-pizzeria restaurants) is consistent with that spl
kept.applies_when: Used to gross up pizzeria-only commercial mass to total pizza mass.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that non-pizzeria channels supply less than 25% or more than 45% of Chicago pizza mass.
